lesson: Today, we work on line breaks. A line break is the spot where a line of the poem stops and your voice pauses for a beat before the next line starts. The break holds one word or thought back for that beat, so you notice it more when it comes. Watch three spots. The poem says the apple's red on one cheek, green on the other. The break makes you wait between the two colors. It says how much is started, nothing finished. The break sets those two states side by side. It says waiting for your hands to pick it back up. The pause before pick it back up lands on the action. The break works because the short wait makes the next word feel like the point. You hear the delay, then the payoff. Try this, break your line right before the word you most want the listener to hear. The second time through count the pauses and hear how so up arrives after them.
